turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize candidates that reproduce the high-efficiency motifs in the training set: fullerene-based ETLs with BCP/Bphen-type selectivity, low-recombination PTAA or NiO-derived HTLs, and reasonably benign Ag/Cu contacts. The strongest candidates are those with close high-performing analogues in the training data.

1. **c030** — This is essentially an exact match to a high-performing training recipe: `IDTT2FPDI | PCBM-60 | Bphen` with `PTAA | PMMA` and Al gave **19.48%**. The layered electron-selective fullerene/PDI/Bphen side and PMMA-passivated PTAA hole contact should suppress interfacial recombination well.

2. **c088** — `C60 | BCP / PTAA / Cu` is a very strong motif: related training devices with this stack reached about **18.6–19.1%**. Willow glass should behave closer to rigid glass than PET, and Cu with BCP/C60 appears favorable in the training set.

3. **c097** — Very close to the high training analogue `ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag` at **18.49%**. The Se analogue should retain the same good energy-level cascade and interfacial passivation, with P3CT-Na providing a selective, low-recombination hole contact.

4. **c044** — `PCBM-60 | BCP / PTAA / Cu` combines a standard selective fullerene/BCP electron contact with one of the best HTLs in the training set. PTAA/Cu variants with C60/BCP are among the top performers, so this should be high even without the extra C60 layer.

5. **c051** — `PCBM-60 | BCP` with `NiO-c | NiO-nw` and Ag is close to the high-performing compact/mesoporous NiO family; the compact NiO layer should block shunts while the nanowire/porous NiO improves hole extraction and contact area.

Final: c030, c088, c097, c044, c051
